title: Rejecting a plaint at the earliest stage - an underused defence
p1:
Many cases spend years in court that could have ended at the very beginning.

The reason? A defence that is often overlooked: rejecting the plaint at the initial stage itself.
p2:
Many people assume that once a lawsuit is filed, the defendant must go through a long trial. But that is not always true.

If the plaint itself fails to disclose a valid cause of action, is legally barred, or does not meet basic requirements, the court can reject it before the case moves forward.
p3:
This is different from proving who is right or wrong. It focuses on whether the case is legally fit to continue.

The practical takeaway: before preparing a long defence, parties should first examine whether the lawsuit itself has a foundation to stand on.

Sometimes, the strongest defence is not fighting a case — it is stopping an unnecessary case at the start.
conclusion: Have you seen a situation where a case could have been avoided if the plaint was challenged at the earliest stage?
